pr.title: Count linguist-generated files as generated in summaries
pr.head: e08f8c85f1ae97aca83482ce1f61ae547859f94e

summary: A summary page sorts each changed file into hand-written, test, generated, or documentation. It counts the lines of each kind and starts every file but a hand-written one collapsed. Before this change, only a file's path decided whether it was generated, through a list of suffixes such as .lock and directories such as gen/. So this repository's compiled site/assets/*.js, which .gitattributes marks linguist-generated and GitHub collapses, showed as hand-written lines on every summary.

Now the linguist-generated attribute decides first, read as GitHub reads it. A file the attributes do not mention falls back to the path list. The attributes come from the pull request's head, because a pull request can change .gitattributes itself.

The site deploy is the hard case. It builds every summary from a shallow checkout of the default branch, which never holds an open pull request's head. So project summary publish reads the head's attributes while it publishes, and stores them on the summaries ref beside the summary as attributes.json. The site build prefers that file. A summary that an earlier release published has no such file, and the build reads the attributes from its own checkout instead.

The head under review merges main into the branch. That merge brings in the publish retry loop, which rebuilds the summaries commit when another publish moves the ref first. The attributes are read once, before that loop, and written on every attempt.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• linguist-generated: a Git attribute that GitHub's Linguist reads. A file with it set is collapsed in a pull request's diff and left out of language statistics.
  • Kind: what a summary shows a file as, the kind field: generated, test, docs, or empty for hand-written.
  • Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden ref that holds each published summary under summaries/<number>/<head>/.
  • git check-attr: the Git command that prints a path's attribute value as set, unset, unspecified, or a string.

cards.title: Where each command reads the attributes
cards.html:
CommandSource
summary publishThe head commit, fetched from the remote if the checkout lacks it; stored as attributes.json
site build, site serveThe stored attributes.json; without one, the --repo-root checkout
summary init, site pageThe checkout they run in

Reading from a checkout uses the head commit when the checkout has it, the working tree when one of its remotes is the pull request's repository, and nothing otherwise.

groups.title: Reading the attribute and deciding a file's kind
groups.kicker: summary.py asks git check-attr for linguist-generated at the head and lets the answer overrule the path.
intro: kind_of decides what a summary shows a file as. It now takes the file's linguist-generated value. True makes the file generated and False keeps it out of that kind, whatever its path says. None means the attributes do not mention the file, and the path list decides as before.

check_attr runs git check-attr so that its answer matches GitHub's. It leaves out the user's global attributes file and the system's, and it matches patterns by exact case even where Git would ignore case. head_attributes reads the attributes of one commit. It uses check-attr --source, which needs Git 2.40, and on an older Git it reads the commit into a scratch index. generated_attributes picks the source for a checkout, as the overview's table shows.

The same file holds publish. publish_attributes reads the head's attributes, fetching the head commit from the remote when the checkout lacks it, and summary_tree writes them into the summary's folder as attributes.json.

files.note: The attribute lookup, the new kind rule, and where publish stores what it read.

checks.text: A file whose attribute is False still falls through to the test and docs checks, so an unmarked gen/check_test.go is a test. test_the_attribute_overrules_the_path covers it.
In a scratch repository, an empty core.attributesFile also turned off the default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes file, not only a file set by name.

Git still reads the checkout's own .git/info/attributes, with --source too. A scratch repository showed it. The docstring's claim that only the repository's .gitattributes files count is slightly too strong. The review lists this as a suggestion.
head reaches --source, read-tree, and the fetch only after FULL_SHA matches it, so a summary's pr.head cannot pass Git an option.

Passing generated={} keeps the validation build from reading attributes a second time. The attributes are then read once, before the retry loop, and every attempt writes the same attributes.json. test_a_retry_after_losing_the_race_keeps_the_heads_attributes covers the retry.

groups.title: The site build prefers the stored attributes
groups.kicker: build_summaries reads attributes.json beside each summary and falls back to its checkout.
intro: build_summaries builds every summary on the summaries ref into the site. For each one, it now passes the stored attributes.json to prepare_page when the file exists. Otherwise it passes the checkout that build_site was given, so a summary from an earlier release still builds and takes the default branch's attributes.
A malformed attributes.json raises SummaryError, so the build skips and reports that one summary, as it does for any other summary that fails.

files.note: Threads the checkout into build_summaries and reads attributes.json beside each summary.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Temporary Git repositories cover each attribute source, the fallbacks, and publish.
intro: GeneratedAttributeTests builds repositories with a root and a nested .gitattributes, and checks exact casing with core.ignoreCase=true, a personal attributes file that must not count, the scratch-index path of an older Git, and the working-tree fallback. Three new PublishTests check that publish stores the head's attributes, fetches a head the checkout lacks, and warns when the remote cannot serve the head. A fourth checks that a publish retry keeps them.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the summarize-pr skill say what counts as generated and where it is read.
intro: docs/cli.md gains a "Generated files" section with the rules and the sources. The summarize-pr skill's SKILL.md and format.md say what counts as generated and that publish stores the head's attributes.
